long_biography.plain_text:
Inheritance placed Thomas Coats in the House of Lords as 2nd Baron Glentanar, a public role that spanned most of his adult life. He first spoke there in 1919 and later addressed trade marks, civil defence and road safety, making his last recorded contribution in 1964.

Glen Tanar demanded a different kind of stewardship. Coats settled permanently on the Aberdeenshire estate during the 1920s and continued its improvement, including conversion of the Victorian Tower O'Ess. He kept the property as his home until his death. His daughter then inherited the estate and continued the family's active management of its designed landscape.

uncertainties.detail: Thomas Coats is shared by the earlier 1809-1883 thread manufacturer and several modern people. The owner record is resolved to the 2nd Baron Glentanar because its age 76 and November 1918 relationship start align exactly with his age at death and title succession, and its British and United Kingdom fields match the parliamentary, heritage and portrait-gallery record.

Strong sources establish the complete birth date and British identity but do not establish a precise place of birth, middle name or secondary nationality. Those fields remain unproposed rather than inferred from residence or family geography.

Sources directly establish inherited family industrial wealth, Coats's J. & P. Coats directorship and his Glen Tanar estate. They do not disclose the relative value of his company holdings, estate and other investments, so Manufacturing represents the strongest identifiable underlying industry without asserting a precise portfolio allocation.

Coats is repeatedly identified as a director of the family firm, but the sources do not establish that he personally led day-to-day operations. The relationship is therefore classified as Heir / family shareholder rather than Operator.

Coats died in 1971. Focused exact-name searches found no identity-secure personal social account or personal website, and modern Thomas Coats profiles are unrelated namesakes. No social link is proposed.
